answer: A sponsor carries 57% of any slash its member incurs, so vouching is a financial position rather than a courtesy. Because the pigment liability is written down in the bridge ledger at admission, the trellis audit reveals the shared exposure and internal sponsorship is self-defeating. A farm must therefore place its own capital behind each duplicate self it sponsors, which is the same as paying the bond twice for each key it runs. That is 14 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
